title: hotfix: fix SLO enforcer race during rapid regional failover causing over-shedding
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Fix: Prevent SLO enforcer double-shedding during rapid regional failover. Improves stability during cross-region failovers and reduces unnecessary load shedding by ensuring atomic region-state transitions and draining in-flight decisions. Backported as hotfix to main.
description: Context: In high-frequency regional failover scenarios we observed the SLO enforcer aggressively shedding capacity in both the originating and fallback regions due to a race between the regional-state transition and the per-request shedding decision queue. This caused prolonged capacity drop and client errors in affected customers. Root cause: the enforcer allowed concurrent state changes while per-region decision queues still contained pending shedding actions. When a region A->B failover was triggered, queued shedding actions for A were applied after the state flip and wrongly targeted B, exacerbating shedding. Change summary: 1) Introduce an atomic per-region state transition token (compare-and-swap) so a single authoritative transition epoch is visible to all workers. 2) Drain and reconcile in-flight shedding decisions on transition: pending decisions are validated against the new epoch and either applied or discarded deterministically. 3) Add hysteresis to the enforcer backoff timer to avoid immediate re-shedding within a short window after failover. 4) Move the critical update path into a single DB-backed transaction (etcd) to ensure cross-worker consistency. 5) Add a deterministic regression test that reproduces the race with simulated high-frequency failovers and add an integration test exercising cross-region routing and load-shedding behavior. Rollout: hotfix is small and guarded by a feature flag (slo_enforcer_atomic_transitions) default-on for main; canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 30 minutes, then 25% for 2 hours before full rollout. Monitoring: new metric slo_enforcer.transition_epoch and per-region pending_decision_rejects; alerting thresholds added to SRE runbook. Impact: reduces unnecessary shedding during rapid failovers and improves application-level success rate during incidents. Actions required: none for customers; SRE to monitor the new metrics during next incident window.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-02-18): Nice repro. Two high-level asks: make sure the epoch token is compact (avoid heavy allocations) and add a comment why we must txn-update the etcd key.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-18): Addressed both: epoch is a uint64 and stored as an atomic counter; added comments and microbenchmark showing negligible allocation.
Priya Natarajan (2026-02-18): Approve after unit test coverage for decision_queue edge cases and CI green.
Diego Alvarez (2026-02-19): Verified integration test reproduces previous failure locally and passes with the fix. Left one nit about log verbosity which I deferred to a follow-up.
